source_excerpt: protocolSection.descriptionModule.detailedDescription and outcomesModule.primaryOutcomes: "NCT01936688" "MK-3222-012" "The base study consists of a screening phase of up to 4 weeks followed by a treatment period of 28 weeks, and a 20-week safety follow-up period off drug." "The base study is divided into 2 sequential parts." "In Part 1 of the base study (Week 0 to Week 12), participants will be randomized to one of 4 study arms (Arm A: MK-3222 200 mg at Week 0 and Week 4 + matching placebo to etanercept twice weekly; Arm B: MK-3222 100 mg at Week 0 and Week 4 + matching placebo to etanercept twice weekly; Arm C: Matching placebo to MK-3222 at Week 0 and Week 4 + matching placebo to etanercept twice weekly; Arm D: Matching placebo to MK-3222 at Week 0 and Week 4 + etanercept 50 mg twice weekly)." "In Part 2 of the base study (Week 12 to Week 28), participants in Arm A, Arm B, and Arm D will receive matching placebo to MK-3222 to maintain blinding at Week 12." "Participants in Arm A and Arm B will continue to receive either MK-3222 200 mg (Arm A) or MK-3222 100 mg (Arm B) at Week 16 and Week 28 and will also receive matching placebo to etanercept once weekly through study Week 28." "At study Week 12, Arm C participants will be re-randomized to receive their first dose of MK-3222 200 mg or MK-3222 100 mg, and will receive additional doses of study medication according to their re-randomized treatment assignment at Week 16 and Week 28." "Participants in Arm C will also receive matching placebo to etanercept once weekly through treatment Week 28." "Participants in Arm D will continue with once weekly doses of etanercept through study Week 28 in combination with matching placebo to MK-3222." "For all participants, completion of Week 28 marks completion of Part 2 and of the overall base study." "Participants originally assigned to Arm D and participants who discontinue treatment prior to completing Part 2 will not be eligible to enroll in the extension." "Participants that are ineligible or opt not to enter the extension study will be encouraged to complete the 20-week follow-up period." "Eligible participants that choose to enroll in the extension study will have an additional treatment period of up to 192 weeks and will be followed for an additional 20 weeks in the follow-up period." "Each participant will receive MK-3222 200 mg or MK-3222 100 mg every 12 weeks up to study Week 220 according to their treatment assignment at the conclusion of Part 2 of the base study." "Proportion of Participants Achieving a Psoriasis Area Severity Index 75% (PASI-75) at Week 12" "Week 12" "Proportion of Participants With a Physician's Global Assessment (PGA) Score of Clear or Minimal With at Least a 2 Grade Reduction From Baseline at Week 12" "Baseline, Week 12" -- The registry describes screening as up to four weeks, not a fixed duration, so screening duration fields are null. The base treatment is Weeks 0–28; the description divides it into Weeks 0–12 and 12–28, with Arm C rerandomized at Week 12. The base safety follow-up is 20 weeks off drug. Eligible participants may enter an optional 192-week extension through Week 220, followed by an additional 20-week follow-up after extension completion; its absolute start week varies with extension participation and is left null. The registry does not establish fixed clinic visit days or a full per-visit schedule table; full_visit_table_available is false because this evidence is narrative registry text. Whole-trial duration and absolute end-of-study week remain null because the screening period is only bounded above and extension participation is optional.

ProDERM statistical methods (PMC7793357): single primary endpoint (TIS >=20 at Week 16) tested at a two-sided alpha=0.05 via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test comparing responder proportions (Octagam vs. placebo) -- no multiple-primary-endpoint gatekeeping procedure (unlike the AD trials' co-primary IGA+EASI-75 hierarchy); secondary endpoints were analyzed descriptively/via ANCOVA and Kaplan-Meier without formal Type-I-error allocation. Sample size: 94 evaluable patients planned for 80% power. Missing data: not imputed except last-observation-carried-forward for the Week-16 ANCOVA when values were missing due to early termination or treatment switch. Both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analysis sets were used.

Extension Period: 6-month open-label Octagam 10% with infusions every 4 weeks (last cycle starting Week 36) through a Week 40 final assessment, with an investigator-discretion dose reduction from 2.0 to 1.0 g/kg available from Week 28 onward for stable/improving subjects. source_excerpt: ProDERM deterioration/escape rules (PMC7793357): "Deterioration was considered confirmed if worsening was observed on 2 consecutive visits," defined as worsening of >=2 cm in Physician's Global Disease Activity (10 cm VAS) AND >=20% worsening in MMT-8; OR >=2 cm global extra-muscular activity worsening; OR >=30% worsening in any 3 of 5 Core Set Measures. At Week 8 or later, confirmed deterioration triggered a blinded switch to the other treatment arm; subjects on Octagam who confirmed deterioration between Week 8-16 were discontinued at the end of the First Period. Switched/rescued subjects were counted as non-responders on the primary Week-16 TIS analysis. This schema's RESCUE shape (topical-then-systemic step-up, as used for the AD trials) does not fit a blinded-crossover escape design; fields describing topical/systemic step-up are left null and the actual switch mechanism is recorded in `rationale` and `trigger_rules`/`flare_definition` as the closest structural fit.

The key secondary endpoints will be analyzed hierarchically: Dichotomized IGA score where treatment success is defined as a 2-step improvement...; Percent change in inflammatory lesion count at Week 12...' Section 11.5.2 Secondary Efficacy Endpoints lists 4 secondary endpoints in order (2-step IGA improvement; percent change in lesion count; Week 8 interim; Week 4 interim) and states: 'Secondary efficacy endpoints will be treated sequentially in the order listed above, at a 0.05 level of significance, only if the co-primary efficacy endpoints are significant.' SAP Section 8.1 restates the co-primary gate: 'both co-primary efficacy endpoints must be significant (ie, attaining significance at the 2-sided 0.05 level without adjustment for multiplicity)' -- i.e., the co-primary pair is tested as a conjunctive (AND) requirement at full unadjusted alpha, and the 4 secondary endpoints are then tested in the pre-specified fixed sequence, each at full 0.05, gated on both co-primaries reaching significance and (implicitly, by fixed-sequence convention) on the preceding endpoint in the sequence being significant. This is a fixed-sequence/serial gatekeeping design, not a Bonferroni/Hochberg-style alpha split.

Note: unlike sibling trials NCT02815267/NCT02815280, this SAP states no non-inferiority step and no per-timepoint superiority cascade for the secondary/tertiary family -- they are gated as a single group behind the co-primary result, not tested in a further internal fixed sequence. source_excerpt: To control for multiple comparisons among the secondary endpoints, the following testing plan will be used: Upon demonstration of statistical significance for S-IGA Success at Week 8, the secondary endpoint of B-IGA Success at Week 8 will be tested hierarchically at the 5% significance level. If the test for B-IGA Success at Week 8 is significant, the alpha of 0.05 will be split to test 2 families of secondary endpoints. The first family will be comprised of the PSSI-75, which will be tested at alpha = 0.03 level. If the test of PSSI-75 is statistically significant, the alpha=0.03 will be used with a Holm testing procedure to test the 4-endpoints of time to success in PSSI-50, CFB in Total PSD score at Week 8, CFB in Total PSD score at Week 4, and PSSI-90 at Week 8. The remaining alpha = 0.02 will be used to test the second family, comprised of the Scalp WI-NRS at Week 8, the Scalp WI-NRS at Week 4, and the Scalp WI-NRS at Week 2. The tests within this second family will be hierarchical, beginning with the endpoint at Week 8, followed by Week 4 and Week 2.

source_excerpt: Protocol FX2016-12 Synopsis (Statistical Methods): 'The co-primary efficacy endpoints will be the dichotomized IGA score... and the absolute change in inflammatory lesion count at Week 12... The key secondary endpoints will be analyzed hierarchically: Dichotomized IGA score where treatment success is defined as a 2-step improvement...; Percent change in inflammatory lesion count at Week 12...' Section 11.5.1 Primary Efficacy Endpoints: co-primary endpoints (absolute change in inflammatory lesion count; dichotomized IGA success), each tested at a two-sided 0.05 level. Section 11.5.2 Secondary Efficacy Endpoints lists 4 secondary endpoints in order (2-step IGA improvement; percent change in lesion count; Week 8 interim; Week 4 interim) and states: 'Secondary efficacy endpoints will be treated sequentially in the order listed above, at a 0.05 level of significance, only if the co-primary efficacy endpoints are significant.' SAP Section 8.1 restates the co-primary gate: 'both co-primary efficacy endpoints must be significant (ie, attaining significance at the 2-sided 0.05 level without adjustment for multiplicity)' -- i.e., the co-primary pair is tested as a conjunctive (AND) requirement at full unadjusted alpha, and the 4 secondary endpoints are then tested in the pre-specified fixed sequence, each at full 0.05, gated on both co-primaries reaching significance and (implicitly, by fixed-sequence convention) on the preceding endpoint in the sequence being significant. Identical design to sister trial FX2016-11 (NCT03142451), same sponsor (Foamix Pharmaceuticals), same drug (FMX103 1.5% minocycline foam vs. vehicle for facial papulopustular rosacea). This is a fixed-sequence/serial gatekeeping design, not a Bonferroni/Hochberg-style alpha split.

source_excerpt: 3.2 Control of Type I Error: "NCT Number: NCT04921969" "For the primary and key secondary analyses, an overall 2-sided Type I error of 0.05 will be used." "A graphical procedure with gatekeeping testing strategy for the primary and key secondary" "analyses will be implemented." "The underlying procedure is derived using the methodology" "developed by Bretz et al (2009)." "The method will guarantee a strong control of the family-wise" "error rate." "In Step 1, 2 families of 4 elementary hypotheses tests at Week 8 are grouped according to" "• Family 1 (1.5% BID vs vehicle):" "− H11: proportion of participants who achieve IGA-TS" "− H12: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "• Family 2 (0.75% BID vs vehicle):" "− H21: proportion of participants who achieve IGA-TS" "− H22: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "Step 2 has 2 families of 4 hypotheses tests:" "• Family 3 (1.5% BID vs vehicle and 0.75% BID vs vehicle on Day 7 Itch NRS):" "− H13: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 7 (Week 1) between 1.5% BID and vehicle" "− H23: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 7 (Week 1) between 0.75% BID and vehicle" "• Family 4 (1.5% BID vs vehicle and 0.75% BID vs vehicle on Day 3 Itch NRS):" "− H14: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 3 between 1.5% BID and vehicle" "− H24: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 3 between 0.75% BID and vehicle" "To control the overall Type I error rate, 2-sided α = 0.05, the Bonferroni's method will be used." "In Step 1, within Family 1 and 2, the endpoints are tested in a fixed sequence at a Bonferronized" "2-sided α = 0.025 level." "The key secondary endpoint will be tested only if the associated primary" "endpoint is rejected." "For any treatment strength, if the 2 related null hypotheses can be rejected," "then the fixed sequence for the other treatment strength can be conducted at the 2-sided α = 0.05" "If all null hypotheses in Family 1 and 2 are rejected, in Step 2, the endpoints in Family 3" "(H13 and H23) will be tested using Bonferroni-Hochberg's procedure with overall 2-sided" "α = 0.05 level." "If both hypotheses in Family 3 are rejected, the endpoints in Family 4 (H14 and" "H24) will be tested similarly using Bonferroni-Hochberg's procedure with overall 2-sided" "α = 0.05 level." -- The SAP describes a graphical gatekeeping strategy with strong familywise control at overall two-sided alpha 0.05. Family 1 and 2 test Week 8 IGA-TS then the associated key secondary endpoint at alpha 0.025, with the stated conditional continuation across strengths; only after both families reject does Step 2 test Family 3, then Family 4 if Family 3 rejects.
